page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance type powered by the Intel Xeon 8163 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. It does not include any local storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage options.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, and falling to the bottom 10% for single-threaded gzip compression. However, the 32 dedicated cores allow multi-threaded performance to reach average levels, as demonstrated by middle-50% rankings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests.

Memory performance is mixed, with read and write bandwidth for large blocks scoring in the average tier, while the Passmark memory score falls into the weak category. For application workloads, the instance achieves average throughput in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and Passmark database operations. It also supports moderate LLM inference speeds, maintaining average prompt processing and text generation speeds for a 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is best suited for workloads that can leverage its 32 physical cores to overcome its weak single-core performance. It is appropriate for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, whereas single-threaded or I/O-heavy local storage workloads may encounter performance bottlenecks.
